name: Bitter Leaf Root Rot
scientificName: Pythium spp., Fusarium spp., Rhizoctonia spp.
description: A soil-borne fungal disease complex that causes root and stem decay in bitter leaf. It is most severe in waterlogged soils and during heavy rains. Infected plants wilt suddenly and collapse as the root system rots away.
symptoms: Sudden wilting of leaves even when soil is moist
Leaves turning yellow then brown from bottom up
Stems near soil level becoming soft and water-soaked
Roots turning brown to black and decaying
Plant collapses and dies within days of first symptoms
causes: Soil-borne fungal pathogens in continuous cropping
Damage to roots from cultivation tools
treatments: Remove and destroy severely affected plants
Improve drainage by creating raised beds
Apply Trichoderma biocontrol agent to soil
prevention: Plant on raised beds or ridges
Rotate with non-host crops like cereals or legumes
Use disease-free planting material from healthy plants
Apply well-decomposed organic matter to improve soil structure
references: University of Ghana Plant Pathology Reports
